Results Experimental and epidemiologic data consistently link short or disturbed sleep with increased incidence of hyperten‑
sion, coronary artery disease, stroke, obesity, type 2 diabetes, and metabolic syndrome. Sleep loss activates the sympathetic 
nervous system and elevates cortisol, while suppressing growth hormone, thereby promoting vasoconstriction, endothelial 
dysfunction, and cardiac remodeling. Parallel disruption of leptin, ghrelin, and endocannabinoid signaling increases hunger, 
caloric intake, and preference for energy‑dense foods, driving weight gain, visceral adiposity, and insulin resistance. Circa‑
dian misalignment from shift work and social jet lag further amplifies inflammatory signaling and metabolic risk across the
